text:
sam: quick heads-up — ran a batch-level profile on prod-like traffic and we're seeing heavy allocator churn in the logits/scratchpad path when short and long seqs are mixed. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/3241 (private)

ingrid: can you paste the allocator trace? is it the freelist or full slab churn? :thinking:

sam: gist of the trace below — frequent alloc/free of ~128KB logits slots and repeated memzero kernels at malloc time. free-list hit rate drops to ~12% during mixed batches.

```
alloc(131072) @ kernel_select:ModelA -> cudaMallocManaged? -> zero_kernel(131072) duration=0.84ms
free(131072) -> put_on_freelist(size=131072) time=0.1ms
alloc(131072) -> miss -> cudaMemset 0.92ms
alloc(512000) -> slab_split -> migrate
free(131072) -> steal_for_prefetch -> removed
```

sam: that's causing ~1.8ms extra per short request on p4d-ish boxes which amplifies at 2k qps.

tara: idea — defer zeroing at allocation time for logits/scratchpads and instead keep returned buffers in a "prefetchable" freelist bucket. before reuse schedule a cheap async kernel to zero only when needed. benefits: avoids paying memset for transient allocations that get reused immediately. downsides: must ensure no stale data escapes (KV pointers).

derek: +1 on deferred-zeroing. also we should separate the freelist into short-lived and long-lived lanes and change batch assignment heuristics so short seqs are preferentially batched together. pseudocode for assignment:

```
if seq_len <= 64: route -> fast_lane_queue
else: route -> bulk_lane_queue
periodically: if fast_lane_queue.size() < min_batch: steal from bulk_lane_queue by size
```

matt: follow-up on KV interactions — logits buffers sometimes hold transient metadata used by KV cache prefetchers. we need a lightweight refcount handshake before we push a buffer back to prefetchable freelist. proposal: add a 1-byte state tag per buffer: {IN_USE, PENDING_RETIRE, PREFETCHABLE}. Components that attach ephemeral refs must mark PENDING_RETIRE and call retire_done() to move to PREFETCHABLE.

ingrid: how expensive is adding that tag? we already have header words. overhead minimal (<1%). risk is races between compute kernels and retire_done ordering. need a small fence in runtime.

sam: ran a microbenchmark of deferred-zero + prefetch freelist on a 8-GPU rack:
perf-bot: synthetic run 3241598800: baseline avg latency short=7.9ms, after-proto short=6.3ms (-20%), p95 baseline=28ms -> 23ms. memzero time % dropped from 14% -> 3%.

perf-bot: full test details: workers=256, mix=70% short(<=64), 30% long(>512), memset_count reduced by 82%, freelist hit from 12%->68%.

tara: nice. next questions: who owns kernel scheduling for the async zero? runtime or kernel-selector? my vote: runtime keeps a small threadpool per device that launches zero kernels with stream priority low. kernel-selector still picks main compute kernel.

matt: also need to ensure quantized kernels that expect packed logits aren't sensitive to stale bytes — add a tiny validation path that flips a tag when zeroing is complete, or make quant kernels tolerant to garbage in padding areas.

derek: rollout plan: 1) add buffer state tag + retire_done handshake (unit tests), 2) implement prefetchable freelist with deferred-zero path behind feature flag, 3) batch-splitting heuristic, 4) perf canary on dedicated ring, 5) enable + monitor OOM/latencies for 48h.

sam: I'll pick up 1+2. tara can take 3, matt will own KV-safety checks and perf validation. ingrid will review the kernel launch/fence bits.

ingrid: one more: add observability hooks — metric for "deferred_zero_count", "prefetch_freelist_hits", and "buffer_state_transitions". also add a tiny eval that runs the eval prompts with 95% short context to ensure quality/regressions.

sam: agree. created a draft PR branch: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/compare/deferred-zeroing-3241 — will push WIP tomorrow.

matt: can you add a tiny stress harness that mixes correlated seq lengths? previous regressions only showed up with correlated sequences.

sam: will do. thanks all :clap:

perf-bot: action items recorded: sam(1,2), tara(3), matt(KV+tests), ingrid(kernel/fence review). canary scheduled in 48h pending PR.
summary: short+long batch mixing causes allocator churn; proposal to defer zeroing and introduce a prefetchable freelist + batch-splitting + buffer state handshake; perf proto shows lower latency and fewer memsets; rollout plan and owners assigned
